pretreatments.description: Subcritical water pretreatment was performed using a semi-continuous flow unit containing a stainless steel hydrolysis reactor (110 mL) with maximum working conditions of 400 °C and 42 MPa. The reactor was heated by an electric system (1500 W) jacket type insulated by ceramic fiber. Water was pumped by a high-pressure pump (double piston pump, model Prep 36 Pump) at 20 mL min^-1. Pressure was controlled by a micrometer valve (Autoclave Engineers, model 10VRMM2812) and maintained at 15 MPa. The temperature was evaluated in two conditions, 170 and 200 °C. The residence time was 20 min, and after this period, the hydrolysates were analyzed according to pH values, reducing sugars, total reducing sugars, the composition of sugars, organic acids, and inhibitors. The solvent/biomass mass ratio was 80 g water per g açai seed. The temperature parameter was evaluated in duplicate, maintaining the flow and pressure parameters constant. Hot hydrolysate was cooled to below 30 °C in a shell-and-tube heat exchanger coupled to a thermostatic bath operating at 10 °C using water as a coolant. The subcritical water pretreatment is considered a pretreatment technique that affects the physical and chemical properties of the biomass to improve its hydrolysis efficiency for anaerobic digestion.
